clue.text: Raised defences for swindle with clever ploys

parts.note: a ramp is British slang for a swindle or racket
arts are cunning tricks or wiles

explanation.surface: Fortifications obtained by fraud and cunning stratagems.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramparts are the earth walls built up around a fort for protection.

clue.text: Paper at fault is in a stew

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
out means wrong, mistaken, as in 'your figures are out'

explanation.surface: A newspaper that has blundered is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a stew' looks like the idiom for being in trouble; 'stew' alone is the definition, with 'is in a' as link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a highly seasoned French meat-and-vegetable dish, a kind of casserole.

clue.text: Why beggar says he won't be a tinker?

definitions.text: Why beggar says he won't be a tinker?

parts.words: Why beggar says he won't be a tinker?
parts.note: a tinker mends pots, so someone who cannot mend might say so, and the phrase broken into words names one who begs

explanation.surface: A vagrant explains why he refuses to work as an itinerant repairer.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as MEND I CAN'T: a tinker mends things, and this beggar admits he can't.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant is a person who lives by begging, such as a friar of a begging order.

clue.text: Find fault with a rule of speech

indicators.note: the words 'a rule' are to be taken as they are said, not spelt

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; a reign is a period of rule by a monarch

explanation.surface: Criticising a regulation about how people talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a reign' spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to accuse or call to account, so it means to censure.

clue.text: Match score

explanation.definitionFit: To tally is to correspond or agree; a tally is also a running count of points.

clue.text: Become established on the bench

explanation.surface: Taking up a regular place on the substitutes' bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle is to put down roots; a settle is also a high-backed wooden bench.

clue.text: Plaudits come in a curious form

indicators.note: the letters of 'come in a' are given a strange new arrangement

explanation.surface: Praise arriving in an unusual shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious form' rearranges COME IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Encomia, the plural of encomium, are formal expressions of high praise.

clue.text: Wild beast may be heard in forest here

indicators.note: signals that the beast's name is to be said aloud

parts.note: the tiger is a big wild cat

explanation.surface: Listen and you might catch a tiger roaring in the woods round here.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic speech TIGER and the answer sound alike; and Siberian tigers do live in this forest.
explanation.definitionFit: The taiga is the vast belt of coniferous woodland across Siberia and northern Canada.

clue.text: Happening to die horribly old in such a home

parts.note: an event is something that happens

indicators.note: the letters of 'die' are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dreadful death for an elderly resident of a care home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges DIE to IDE. The definition is cryptic: an 'eventide home' is a British name for an old people's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide means evening, and figuratively the last stage of life, hence homes for the elderly.

clue.text: British people look down on rented jewellery

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting above another is said to look down on it

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
let means rented out

explanation.surface: Snobbish Britons scorn hired trinkets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look down on' places RACE above LET in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is an ornamental band worn round the wrist, an item of jewellery.

clue.text: Normal procedures for professional career

explanation.surface: Standard methods for anyone pursuing a profession.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means usual custom, and is also the work of a family doctor or GP.

clue.text: The benefit of public service

explanation.surface: The advantage of state-run provision.
explanation.definitionFit: Utility means usefulness, and a utility is a company supplying gas, water or power.

clue.text: Firm agreement

explanation.definitionFit: Compact means solid and dense; a compact is also a pact or treaty.

clue.text: Savage throws writer into the water

indicators.note: together with 'into', this asks for one piece to be tossed inside another
with 'throws', puts the writer within the waterway

parts.note: a canal is a man-made stretch of water
a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: A brute flings an author into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throws' and 'into' work together as one container signal; 'the' is a link before the waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannibal is a person who eats human flesh, the archetypal savage of old adventure stories.

clue.text: Genuinely in bed, of a fever

indicators.note: the fodder words are thrown into a feverish jumble

explanation.surface: Truly laid up in bed with a temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fever' rearranges IN BED OF A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'in good faith', used to say something is real and sincere.

clue.text: River feeding into one drain, but no rain is discharged

indicators.note: a river feeds into the sea, so the river letter flows into the rest

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or dice

indicators.note: the letters of 'rain' are to be removed from the word drain

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stream flows into a gutter that, oddly, carries no rainwater away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but no rain' leaves D from DRAIN; 'feeding into' puts R inside ACED. The definition refers to electricity jumping a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical current that has arced has leapt across a gap as a spark.

clue.text: Caught by sin — vital elements in his theology

definitions.text: Caught by sin — vital elements in his theology

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the component letters of the fodder are broken up and put together afresh

explanation.surface: Being trapped by sin is a central component of this man's beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elements' is an unusual anagram signal: the component letters are broken up. The whole clue also describes the reformer's doctrine of human depravity.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of John Calvin held that humanity is fallen and that salvation is by grace alone.

clue.text: Put through torment — sacred for Japanese?

indicators.note: Japanese speakers are said to swap the sounds of L and R, so the Ls become Rs

parts.note: hallowed means holy or sacred

explanation.surface: Tortured over something holy to the Japanese.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke relies on the stereotype that Japanese speakers render L as R.
explanation.definitionFit: To be harrowed is to be deeply distressed, as a field is torn by a harrow.

clue.text: Cart one perhaps used for carrying goods

indicators.note: suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cart may be employed for transporting things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CART plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: An artic, short for articulated lorry, is a large truck hauling freight.

clue.text: Best loved son goes into cupboard

indicators.note: one piece entering another, as a son walks into the cupboard

parts.note: a closet is a cupboard or small storeroom

explanation.surface: The favourite boy hides in the wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes into' puts S inside CLOSET.
explanation.definitionFit: The closest friend is the dearest, most intimate one.

clue.text: On the contrary, think nothing of it

explanation.surface: A modest disclaimer in reply to thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic denial, and also a polite reply waving away gratitude.

clue.text: Local, very hot, abandoning run

indicators.note: the run letter is left behind, dropped from the word for hot

parts.note: tropical weather is sweltering
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood suffering a heatwave gives up on jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket scoring abbreviates run as R.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical originally means confined to one place, as in a topical ointment, hence local.

clue.text: It's not often that an upturn in current fashions brings in money

indicators.note: the turned word takes the money letter inside it
in a down clue, an upturn reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: modes are prevailing styles
L stands for the pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Rarely does a trendy revival earn any cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upturn' turns MODES to SEDOM; 'brings in' puts L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom means rarely, on few occasions.

clue.text: Censure work on raincoat

explanation.surface: Criticism of a job repairing a mackintosh.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-PROOF, to waterproof a coat again.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a rebuke; to re-proof is to treat fabric again against rain.

clue.text: Block up initially a shrew's home

parts.note: a pad is a block of writing paper

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word up is used

explanation.surface: First seal off the burrow of a small rodent-like animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The shrew is Katharina of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew, set in this Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comedy of the tamed termagant takes place in this northern Italian city.

clue.text: Dispossess of a pawn in draw

indicators.note: places the chess letter inside the other word

parts.note: to derive is to draw or obtain from a source
P is the chess notation for pawn

explanation.surface: Losing a pawn while the chess game is a stalemate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' looks like a chess result but means obtain.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprive someone is to take something away from them.

clue.text: Make money abroad, as the senior member

parts.note: to do is to make, as in do a meal
the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: The eldest partner earns cash overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most respected or longest-serving person in a group.

clue.text: Woeful young Sheffield supporter?

explanation.surface: A gloomy youngster cheering for a Yorkshire football team.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme says 'Wednesday's child is full of woe'; Sheffield Wednesday is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme assigns woe to a weekday's infant, and a young fan of the club is one too.

clue.text: Scarcity put right in the end

indicators.note: with 'in', asks for one letter to be placed within a word
with 'put', places the right letter inside

parts.note: death is the end of life

explanation.surface: A shortage finally corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put ... in' puts R inside DEATH.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a lack or shortage of something.

clue.text: Slave sharing the grey mare?

parts.note: in the Devon folk song Widecombe Fair, a crowd of men borrow Tom Pearse's grey mare; one of them shares his name with Stowe's enslaved hero

explanation.surface: A bondsman taking turns on a borrowed horse.
explanation.walkthrough: In the song Widecombe Fair, 'Uncle Tom Cobley and all' ride the grey mare; the answer is also the slave in Harriet Beecher Stowe's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Stowe's anti-slavery novel is an enslaved man, and the song's last rider bears that name.
